issue: #405 (CRUX audit E03) — sign --verify, sign --pq --verify and lock-verify-hmac never read the signature they verified

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: digest --verify and lock-audit still pass on a hash the attacker controls, so the branch fails verification on every remaining path — REFUTED: digest is documented in its module header and help as tamper evidence with no key; it claims no verification to fail. The keyed check is lock-verify-sig.

The right fix was to implement real signatures (option a) rather than withdraw the verbs (option b) — REFUTED: there was no key material and no key-distribution answer; a real signature under the old flags would ship the hard part unanswered. Subtraction leaves one honest keyed verb and one honest unkeyed one.

lock_verify_sig_rejects_a_one_byte_mutation is a falsifier of this change — REFUTED: it was green before the change and is labelled a regression guard in the file; the falsifiers are the five that go red with src/ reverted plus the algorithm-echo case.
quorum.divergence: the probe lane confirmed the subtraction and the algorithm-echo fix; the agy lane found a dead tamper-detection block in lock-audit and an over-broad withdrawal helper in the test (both taken) and charged the unkeyed verbs with failing a claim they do not make (refuted).

systems: Sigstore/cosign — key and algorithm from Fulcio/Rekor or the operator; nothing self-reported in the artifact is trusted
TUF — keys, algorithms and thresholds pinned in an out-of-band root.json; a target is trusted only through that root
git commit signing (gpg/ssh) — the key id in the signature is a lookup hint into a local keyring or allowed_signers; trust lives in the keyring
Debian apt Release/InRelease — the hashes in Release are trusted only after the detached signature verifies against /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/
crux.verdict: every surveyed verifier obtains its key and algorithm out of band and trusts nothing the artifact says about itself. A verb that read a signature field and checked a hash was below that bar; a keyed verb that takes its key from the operator and an unkeyed verb that says so are at it.

known_limits: This is a breaking CLI change: `sign`, `sign --pq` and `lock-verify-hmac` are gone and `<recipe>.sig.json` becomes `<recipe>.digest.json`. Documented in CHANGELOG and the book; there is no compatibility shim by design.

`lock-verify-sig` binds a lock to a shared secret via blake3(lock ++ key), which is a MAC, not a signature: anyone who can verify can also sign. An asymmetric scheme with a key-distribution story is a separate ticket.
`lock-sign --key` still takes the secret from argv on this branch; #408 (E13) moves it off argv and lands separately.
